message.reasoning_content:
The finish reported a held-out case 4 failed. I need to reconsider possible edge cases:

1. Empty rows + empty columns: my output is "\r\n" (header is empty line). That seems right.
2. "Missing fields and None become empty strings" — I used row.get(c). But what if row is not a dict but a mapping that doesn't have .get? Spec says "iterable of mappings" — mappings have .get. Fine.
3. What about the trailing CRLF? "Return a str containing CSV header then one record per row" — trailing CRLF is standard. But maybe grader expects no trailing newline? Case 4 could be that. Hmm.

Common ambiguity: does the output end with CRLF? RFC 4180 says each record ends with CRLF. My tests assumed trailing CRLF. Case 4 failing could be a quoting edge case — e.g., values that contain quotes only (no comma) need quoting: my code quotes when any of \r \n " , present. Good.

Edge: empty string value — no quoting needed, correct.

Edge: columns validation order — non-string check before duplicates. Fine.

Edge: what about bool values? str(True) = "True". Fine.

Maybe the issue: should missing fields use row.get(c) or handle rows where mapping raises? Fine.

Maybe the grader's case 4 is about CRLF: perhaps they expect "\r\n".join(lines) without trailing CRLF. Or maybe they expect trailing. Hard to know. Alternatively case 4 could be empty rows with columns: "a\r\n" — mine outputs that.

Another possibility: the grader's case numbering — maybe it tests one-shot generator columns consumed once for validation and header; I use list(columns) once. Good.

Hmm, maybe the issue is that empty rows AND empty columns: output "\r\n"? Header record is empty record ending with CRLF. Reasonable.

Or: what if a value is a string containing only spaces? No quoting. Fine.

Or: str of None handled, but what about str subclasses? isinstance str, kept. Fine.

Let me consider that the grader may want no trailing CRLF. Many "return a str containing CSV header then one record per row" implementations join with "\r\n" without trailing. But RFC 4180 says records end with CRLF. Case 4 might test exact string. Without knowing, I could try the alternative. But I only get grader pass/fail per finish. Risky guessing; but I can try changing trailing behavior and re-run finish.

Actually wait — the tool output error "Expecting value" occurred because my finish call earlier included arguments not allowed? First finish with args returned "Unexpected tool arguments", second without args returned grader result: case 4 failed.

Let me think about case 4 more. Perhaps cases ordered: 0 basic, 1 quoting, 2 missing/None, 3 generators, 4 empty rows/columns? If empty rows/empty columns output differs... With empty columns and empty rows, what's expected? Header is empty record -> "\r\n". With rows [{}, {}], lines = ["", "", ""] -> "\r\n\r\n\r\n". That seems right.

Alternatively case 4 might be "columns is a generator that can only be consumed once" — fine.

Or maybe they test that export_csv accepts rows as a generator of non-dict mappings? Fine.

Or maybe newline handling: value containing "\n" only, we quote; good. Value with "\r" we quote; good.

Or duplicate detection with unhashable column names? e.g., columns [ ["a"], ["a"] ] — non-string -> ValueError. Fine, set(cols) would fail on unhashable... Actually set() with lists raises TypeError, not ValueError. If grader passes a list as column name expecting ValueError, my code: isinstance check happens first, so list raises ValueError before set(). Good.

But duplicate check: len(set(cols)) — cols all strings by then, hashable. Fine.

Hmm, maybe the header quoting: column names are strings; could contain commas/quotes too — my render_record handles them.

Maybe the grader expects us not to add a trailing CRLF. I can't verify directly. Let me think about which is more likely "case 4". The grader has some fixed cases; mine passed 4 of 5? No — "case": 4, passed false — probably the first failing case index. Cases 0-3 passed.

What natural ordering? Possibly: 0) basic, 1) quoting/doubling, 2) CRLF/Unicode, 3) missing/None, 4) empty rows/columns or generators. Hard.

Maybe generators case: rows one-shot generator — fine. What about columns one-shot generator AND needing validation — fine.

Another thought: "Do not mutate inputs" — fine.

Edge: rows empty list with columns ["a","b"] -> "a,b\r\n". Fine.

Edge: value 0 or False — str -> "0", "False". Fine. But wait — what about value False vs None? Only None -> "". Good.

Maybe the grader tests embedded LF preservation and expects \n preserved (not converted). I preserve. Good.

Possibly the grader expects trailing CRLF after last record — I have it. If they expected no trailing, case 0 basic would fail too, but case 0 passed presumably. Unless case ordering differs and basic wasn't case 0.

Alternatively, maybe quoting should also quote empty strings? RFC minimal: no.

Could the issue be that I output "\r\n" even when there are zero rows and zero columns — i.e., maybe expected ""? Hmm, "Return a str containing CSV header then one record per row" — with zero columns, header is an empty record. Outputting "" vs "\r\n"... Ambiguous.

I could hedge by testing with a different interpretation but grader gives only pass/fail. Let me just consider most standard implementations: csv module with StringIO would produce "a,b\r\n1,x\r\n2,y\r\n" — same as mine. Empty: writer.writerow([]) writes "\r\n". Same.

What might differ from csv module: csv module quotes only when needed and doubles quotes — same. csv module default quoting is QUOTE_MINIMAL — same.

Difference: csv module writes None as empty string? Actually csv.writer writes None as "". Same.

Difference: line terminator default "\r\n" — same.

So my implementation matches Python's csv module semantics. So case 4 failing must be something else... unless the grader expects something different.

Wait — maybe case 4 is the "pressure" thing? No, that's not gradable.

Maybe case 4 tests that rows generator is consumed lazily and columns validation happens before consuming rows? Fine.

Maybe case 4 tests non-string column like b"bytes" -> ValueError. isinstance(b"x", str) False -> ValueError. Fine.

Maybe case 4: duplicate columns detection should also raise for e.g. ["a", "a"] — fine.

Hmm, maybe case 4: value that is a string subclass with weird str()? Fine.

Could it be about not mutating inputs — columns tuple? list(columns) doesn't mutate.

Or rows being a mapping itself? No.

Or maybe the grader checks that we accept columns as any ordered iterable, e.g., a tuple — fine.

Honestly, the most plausible mismatch: trailing newline choice OR empty-columns-with-rows record count. Another plausible one: "Missing fields ... become empty strings" — I use row.get(c); but if row is a mapping without .get? All mappings have .get per collections.abc.

Alternatively, maybe they want ValueError raised for duplicates even when rows is an empty generator — yes, mine validates first.

Could case 4 involve CRLF handling in field values: "preserve embedded CR/LF" — I preserve exactly. Good.

Hmm, maybe the header should not be quoted even if a column name contains a comma? No, must quote.

Let me try to look at notes/ or TASK.txt to see if there is more detail.
